Messages.Author: masika
Messages.Body:
Last Stand
Unique Master, 6 (!) pool:
Put this card in play. When any other Methuselah is ousted, the
current turn ends, and this card is burned. The predator of the ousted
Methuselah (if more than one was ousted, go clockwise from the left of
the Methuselah whose turn just ended) takes the next turn.

This is just to ask what this card is supposed to do?

Costing 6 pool I'd imagine something worth the effort.
Multiple reading still left me under the impression it's
crap. Who'd spend 6 pool to give a meth (if you're lucky
it's you) an extra turn?

Did I miss something?

I dont think I'd include it in a deck if it would cost
half the pool.

Cheers, Alf

So you can tap out and take down your prey.. and then have a full turn
to go at your new prey. It makes Stealth Bleed even more dangerous, as
if it needed it... Or you can use that extra turn to "become a wall", and
be all untapped and defensive for your predator to come at you.

The cost of 6 is just a pre-emptive "you won't gain 6 from your next
oust", sort of. You really shouldn't play this card except on the Master
Phase of the turn that you think you'll oust your prey.

Messages.Author: Ira
Messages.Body:
Last Stand can also be potentially very useful in a timed tournament
environment; getting to take two turns in a row can allow a game win,
when other people were counting on getting an extra turn.

I highly praise this card because it opens up a new gameplay mechanic
that never existed before in this game; it's high risk, high reward.

Also note that when someone gets ousted, the current turn ends
immediately (so no finishing your minion phase, influence, or
discard.) I imagine interesting decisions when that card is in play,
I have 3 minions, and my prey is all tapped out with 1 pool. Do I
hunt twice, and then bleed? Or do I bleed first, and then end up
wasting the actions of the other two minions? This card generates
interesting gameplay, and thus I praise it.

It's really hard for me to know if it's balanced; it actually seems a
little too expensive. Or maybe just that the minion phase should end
immediately, but still allow influence and/or discard. *shrug* I
didn't playtest it so I don't know - I'll put my faith in the
playtesters, and try this out when I get the chance.

Bravo to the designer,

Ira
